sources.title: Lata Mangeshkar (Q156347), verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-25): label 'Lata Mangeshkar', description 'Indian singer (1929-2022)', born 1929-09-28, died 2022-02-06, P18 image 'Lata Mangeshkar - still 29065 crop.jpg'. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Lata Mangeshkar', read in full. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: playback singer for the soundtracks of more than 2,000 Indian films over eight decades; classical training from her father and from Aman Ali Khan and Amanat Khan; early difficulty gaining a foothold against the prevailing heavier voices; first hit in Andaz (1949); music directors such as Naushad, Madan Mohan and S. D. Burman composed to use her range; Guinness 'most recorded artist' entry in 1974; Padma Bhushan, Dadasaheb Phalke Award, Padma Vibhushan, Bharat Ratna (2001) and the Legion of Honour. Reference entry: factual and admiring.

Al Jazeera obituary, 'Nightingale of India Lata Mangeshkar has died' (6 February 2022), read in full: more than half a century of dominance in Bollywood music, work with nearly all of the major music directors, her willingness to take a stand on fees and a share of royalties, the habit of writing out each song by hand before recording, longevity and discipline, and critics' complaint that her dominance left little room for newer singers. International news obituary with a quoted music author; mostly admiring, with one critical line.

Songlines magazine obituary by Katherine Schofield, 'Lata Mangeshkar (1929-2022)' (7 February 2022), read in full: the 1949 Mahal broadcast that drew listeners to All India Radio asking whose voice it was, her classical training and high, clear timbre as the sound of the film heroine, the later singers who imitated her style, her duets with Mohammed Rafi, and her 'hard-nosed business acumen', refusal to sing vulgar parts and power to make or break films and music directors. A specialist-magazine obituary by a music historian: admiring in register but analytical, and the source that states the business side most directly.

The News Minute, 'Legendary singer Lata Mangeshkar passes away at 92' (6 February 2022), read in full: career chronology, the break she got from music director Ghulam Haider in an era that preferred slightly nasal voices, the 1949 Mahal hit, the range of music directors and male co-singers, and the list of awards. Regional news obituary used for the career timeline and for how her break came; the health and death passages were not used.

Daily Times (Pakistan, 13 March 2014) article on Muhammad Rafi, republished by the Academy of the Punjab in North America, read in full. COUNTER-VOICE: relays a columnist's account that Rafi disagreed with Mangeshkar over her push for singers to receive royalties, that they stopped singing duets, that the composer Jaikishan later patched things up, and that she was annoyed by a letter disputing her Guinness song count. Opinion column about Rafi that itself relies on another writer's article; one account of one episode, treated as a single secondhand voice from Rafi's side and not as proof of her motives.

Partho Datta, review of Nasreen Munni Kabir's 'Lata Mangeshkar: In Her Own Voice', The Book Review (December 2009), read as far as the free preview goes (the rest is behind a login): the reviewer's recollection of a concert where she looked at a notebook throughout because she held that the words matter as much as the music, his view that her fire was reserved for recorded music and that she re-invented herself in the 1970s, and his note that Kabir's interview is respectful and avoids controversy while Raju Bharatan's book was more critical. Partly read: later paragraphs were not opened.

Rolling Stone India, review of 'Lata Mangeshkar in Her Own Voice' by Nasreen Munni Kabir (25 July 2009), read in full. COUNTER-VOICE: praises the book's care over facts but notes that Kabir avoids difficult areas, including the 'Mangeshkar monopoly' and complaints about its effect on other singers, and says the later half is encomium after encomium. A critical book review: used to bound the evidence and to flag that the well-known biographies are respectful or partisan.
Wikimedia Commons file page 'Lata Mangeshkar - still 29065 crop.jpg' (photograph by Bollywood Hungama, CC BY 3.0, with a Wikimedia volunteer-team permission record), checked for the portrait only.

mastery_orientation.rationale: [src_lata_brit, src_lata_songlines, src_lata_aljazeera | childhood to 2000s | reference + specialist obituary + news] She was trained in classical singing from age five by her father and by Aman Ali Khan and Amanat Khan (Britannica), which Songlines credits for the extraordinary flexibility of her voice, and she kept recording for film for some six decades. The sources describe training and a long career rather than her own practice habits in detail, and all are retrospective and admiring, so this is documented training with a moderate-confidence reading of mastery as an orientation.

discipline.rationale: [src_lata_aljazeera, src_lata_songlines, src_lata_tnm | 1940s-2000s | news obituaries + specialist obituary] Al Jazeera pairs longevity with discipline and says she wrote out each song by hand before recording; Songlines and The News Minute describe consistent recording across more than a thousand films over about six decades. The handwritten-lyrics habit is a single reported detail and the word 'discipline' is the obituarist's, so this is read as an inference from sustained output and a stated routine.

detail_orientation.rationale: [src_lata_aljazeera, src_lata_datta | recording and concert practice | news + book review] She wrote each song out by hand before recording (Al Jazeera) and looked at a notebook of lyrics throughout concerts, which she justified by saying words are as important as the music (Datta, recalling a concert). Both are small, retrospective observations and Datta's review is only partly read, so the claim is limited to care for the words of a song.

adaptability.rationale: [src_lata_brit, src_lata_songlines, src_lata_datta, src_lata_tnm | 1940s-2000s | reference + specialist obituary + review] She stayed in demand across successive generations of heroines and music directors, from Nargis and Madhubala to Preity Zinta (Britannica, The News Minute), and Datta describes her re-inventing herself in the 1970s as the voice of a new generation of heroines. Songlines notes later singers had to imitate her style, which suggests the industry adapted to her as well; the evidence shows long relevance rather than how she personally changed her approach, so confidence is moderate.

persistence.rationale: [src_lata_brit, src_lata_tnm | 1942-1949 | reference + news] Britannica says she struggled in her early years to establish herself as a playback singer when heavier voices were preferred, and The News Minute dates her first notable break to Ghulam Haider and the 1948-1949 films before the Mahal hit. Only the career struggle is used; the sources do not describe how many auditions or refusals she faced, so this is a modest inference.

social_assertiveness.rationale: [src_lata_aljazeera, src_lata_songlines, src_lata_apna | 1960s onward | news obituary + specialist obituary + opinion column] Al Jazeera says she was not shy about taking a stand on raising her fees or asking for a share of royalties, and Songlines describes her 'hard-nosed business acumen', refusal to sing vulgar parts and power to make or break films and music directors. The royalties stance is a documented professional position; critics (Al Jazeera, Rolling Stone India) say her dominance crowded out other singers, hence dual-edged.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: [src_lata_apna, src_lata_songlines | early 1960s | opinion column + specialist obituary] One columnist account says her royalties disagreement with Mohammed Rafi ended their duets for a period until a composer mediated, and Songlines mentions her duets with Rafi alongside her business stance. The only detailed account is a secondhand opinion column that relays another writer's article and comes from Rafi's side; the sources differ elsewhere on duration, so this is a bounded inference about holding a professional position at the cost of a working relationship. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): first set at 70 / 0.5, lowered to 60 / 0.42 because the only detailed account is a single secondhand column that I could not corroborate from an independent source, so the trait claim was stronger than the documented behaviour.

portrait.source: Wikimedia Commons file 'Lata Mangeshkar - still 29065 crop.jpg': photograph of Lata Mangeshkar by a Bollywood Hungama photographer at an event (the file page names the source still as the launch of a painting collection), a cropped image on the Bollywood Hungama website; the original file is 440 x 400 pixels, saved unchanged (no resizing, no upscaling). Licensed CC BY 3.0 by the copyright holder, with a Wikimedia volunteer-team permission record (ticket 2008030310010794) and a review by a Commons administrator in August 2010 who confirmed the image was on the Bollywood Hungama site. The file page gives the date as 2008; the first upload recorded the date as unknown, so the year is the file page's statement only.
portrait.creator: Bollywood Hungama

PERSPECTIVES: reference (Britannica); international and regional news obituaries; a music-historian obituary; a Pakistani opinion column from Rafi's side (counter-voice); two reviews of the Kabir interview book (one critical of its omissions). NOT OPENED: Kabir's book itself and Raju Bharatan's and Harish Bhimani's biographies (lending or unavailable; known only through reviews), the full Datta review (login wall), the Guardian, BBC and Scroll pieces (HTTP 404 at the guessed URLs), The Week interview (access denied), Moneylife Part 3 (page text not usable). SOURCE-DEPTH CAVEAT: all behavioural evidence reaches this file through obituaries, reviews and one opinion column; no biography or interview text was read directly, so confidence is capped at 0.55 and no row exceeds 74. The royalties dispute with Rafi is a documented professional episode but its detail rests on a single secondhand column; sources disagree on its length and cause and it is treated as a counter-voice and a bounded inference only. PORTRAIT_PREFLIGHT: plausible (lead) / confirmed: the Commons page gives author Bollywood Hungama, CC BY 3.0, a permission-record ticket and an admin review; the permission text limits use to event photos by Bollywood Hungama photographers of Bollywood events, which matches this file's stated source (an event). The Bollywood Hungama site itself was not opened for a conflicting notice. The image is a small crop (440 x 400, no larger original), a likeness photograph of her in later life. One alternative, the Commons headshot from a 2015 Bollywood Hungama photo, is only 196 x 166 and was rejected on size; other category images were not reviewed. SELF-CALIBRATION: top-risk rows social_assertiveness (kept, two independent obituaries state the royalties stance) and conflict_tolerance (lowered, see its rationale) and mastery_orientation (kept: training is documented by a reference source and a specialist obituary); one row lowered.
